conflict_topics: whether to ask the leaver to change her chosen restaurant
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants present clear, ordinary workplace arguments (honor leaver's choice vs inclusivity).
Noticeable repetition of the line 'he said he's fine' (Turns 22, 23, 25, 28, 31), which is used as a closure device.
Roles and facts are consistent (who chose the restaurant, dietary constraint, timing); no role confusion.
evaluation.final_reason: No agreement was reached. Agent C consistently argued that the lunch venue must allow all team members to eat together and proposed asking the leaver for a second-choice (Turn 14: 'Why don't we ask her for a second-choice spot?'). Agents A, B, and D consistently defended keeping the leaver's chosen Korean barbecue and emphasized Agent D's stated willingness to attend despite not eating (e.g. Turn 15: 'Agent D already said he doesn't mind.'; Turn 22: Agent D: '...Let's just go where she wants to go.'). The transcript ends with these opposing positions intact and no mutual acceptance of a concrete alternative.
position_change_notes: No participant substantially changed position during the run: C consistently insisted on finding a venue where everyone can eat; A consistently defended the leaver's choice; D consistently said he would attend despite not eating; B moved from neutral inquiry to supporting going where the leaver wanted (Turn 8: '...we should go where she wants to go').
A repeated the refusal to ask the leaver to change (Turns 15, 18, 20, 23), indicating no softening.
C repeatedly proposed a compromise (asking for a second choice) and did not withdraw the demand.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 2: Agent B: 'Ah, she'll be happy.' Turn 3: Agent C asks others if the place is okay. No incompatible positions expressed yet.

Turn 4: Agent D: 'Sorry, I can't eat there. It's not halal. But I can just come along for the company.' Turn 5: Agent C: 'No, that's no good, Agent D. We should find somewhere we can all eat.' A clear disagreement about whether the team should go to the chosen restaurant.

Turn 7: Agent A defends the leaver's choice: 'It's her farewell, and she chose the place.' Turn 8: Agent B supports going. Positions are aligning (A/B) against C's objection; conflict intensified but not yet entrenched.

Turn 9: Agent C: 'The point is to eat together. Agent D can't eat at all...' Turn 10: Agent D again: 'Really, it's fine. The main thing is being there...' The same incompatible positions persist without settlement.

Turn 11: Agent C: 'You'd just be sitting there watching us eat. That's not a proper team lunch.' Turn 13: Agent A: 'But she was really happy when I told her we were going there.' The opposition is sharper and more principled, increasing intensity.

Turn 14: Agent C proposes asking the leaver for a second-choice. Turn 15: Agent A: 'We can't ask her to change it now... Agent D already said he doesn't mind.' The disagreement remains; a proposed compromise was rejected.

Turn 18 (A) repeats refusal to change: 'We can't ask her to change it now...' Turn 19 (C): 'He's just being polite... We can find somewhere else nearby that works for everyone.' C intensifies challenge to the status quo, increasing conflict.

Turn 20: Agent A: 'It's her farewell, not a regular team lunch.' Turn 22: Agent D: 'Please, don't worry about it. Let's just go where she wants to go.' Positions persist: A/B/D favor keeping the plan; C opposes.

Turn 23: Agent A: 'See? He's said it again. Let's just go with the plan.' Turn 24: Agent C: '...Are we really going to sit there and eat a meal in front of him? That's not a farewell lunch...' C's language grows more forceful, widening the divide.
Turn 25 and Turn 28: Agent A repeatedly defends D's stated consent: 'He said he's fine... He's an adult, Agent C.' The core incompatibility (venue vs inclusivity) remains unresolved.

Turn 29: Agent C: 'This isn't about me deciding for him. It's about what's right. He's being polite...' Turn 30: Agent A: 'So what Agent D says doesn't matter, only what you think is 'right'?' The exchange becomes more accusatory and entrenched.

Turn 31: Agent B: 'She's right. He's said he's fine.' Turn 32: Agent C: 'So we're just going to sit and watch him not eat? Is everyone really okay with that?' Final turn maintains the unresolved disagreement over whether to honor the leaver's choice or find an alternative.

substantive_insights: Tension between respecting the departing colleague's preference and ensuring inclusive participation for all team members.
Agent D's willingness to attend but not eat complicates the question of what counts as an acceptable team lunch (presence vs shared eating).
Politeness may mask real discomfort: several agents (notably C) interpret D's acceptance as politeness rather than genuine consent, which motivates the push for an alternative.
Timing (the leaver's last day is 'tomorrow') is invoked by A to argue against changing plans; C views the timing as still adequate to adjust.
